svg.text: ENUMERATION-AWARE SURVEY: 200 ms PROBES, DEPTH-FIRST CONTACT

text.tspan: 4 rounds x 3 occupied slots x 200 ms
Ordered first-contact opportunities; actual Channel 9 delivery remains custody driven
Collection and pair ranging continue until data-complete or the 30 min safety
Listen except exact slot 0 in every round
Success, RAM custody, or randomized recovery; never transmit early
Listen except exact slot 1 in every round
Pre-RF wait; no retry is consumed
Success, RAM custody, or randomized recovery
Listen except exact slot 2 in every round
Pre-RF wait; no retry is consumed
Success, RAM custody, or randomized recovery
All three direct anchors have had an uncontended first opportunity

No ACCEPT: one randomized retry at the same parent, then each alternate route. Only after known routes are exhausted: route discovery plus a longer randomized backoff. Relays stay silent when unavailable.
Collecting reports x/N; countdown uses slot span S, anchor count N, and maximum depth D
Pair plan tightens the estimate; an overrun shows 'Over estimate by ... -
Hard rule: a probe stays inside its exact stable enumeration slot. Soft rule: a child delays only
its first connection attempt, ordered by hop depth and then stable slot. The relay keeps no
child roster and sends no BUSY reply. Existing one-upstream plus one-downstream ownership, RAM
custody, retries, route fallback, and gateway proof remain responsible for delivery.
all matching anchors enter the same Ch5
all radios leave the exclusive probe
second direct anchor gets its first
third direct anchor gets its first
this is not a survey timeout

Three-anchor D-F1-F2 example, relative to the shared probe start. The START delivery and preparation barrier happens before t=0. Four rounds of exact 200 ms Channel-5 slots finish at 2.4 s. Later Channel-9 cells use the implemented 2270 ms report-service allowance. Retries, alternate routes, and pair work may continue past the right edge.
